# Does Prior Coding Experience Affect How Students Experience COMP110?

## The Idea

Our objective was to investigate whether there is any significant difference between those students who enter the COMP110 class with some programming experience compared to those who enter without having any prior knowledge of programming. In other words, are those with prior programming knowledge able to perform better and understand the subject matter better? Furthermore, are they more likely to recommend the course?

The answer to this question is affirmative. If the non-programmers are experiencing more difficulty with the course, then it should indicate that there is need to include additional support for non-programming students. For example, this could involve additional practice exercises, office hours aimed towards beginners, or introductory materials.

## The Analysis

Data obtained from the COMP110 student survey conducted early in the semester was utilized. The student survey questioned the students on their previous experience with computer programming, which varied from under a month to more than 2 years. Other questions included their perceived difficulty of the course, level of understanding, and recommendations for the course, each question rated on a scale of 1 to 7.

## Visualizations

### Average Understanding Score by Experience Level

Experienced students understood the course better compared to the beginner students. Those with less than one month of experience had an average of 4/7 while those with more than two years had an average of 5.5.

<img src="/static/imgs/chart1.png" alt="bar chart showing average understanding score by prior experience level" width="700"/>

### Difficulty vs. Understanding Across Experience Levels

If we plotted the results for difficulty and understanding in the same graph, we would see how the two were oppositely correlated with increasing experience – difficulty decreased while understanding increased.

<img src="/imgs/chart2.png" alt="line plot comparing difficulty and understanding scores across experience levels" width="700"/>

### Would Recommend Scores by Experience Level

Despite the increase in difficulty for the beginners, the would_recommend results were very high in all the experience groups. It seemed that most students, irrespective of their experience, recommended that other students take COMP110.

<img src="/static/imgs/chart3.png" alt="box plot showing would recommend scores by prior experience level" width="700"/>

## Conclusion

My results partially confirmed my hypothesis. It seems that previous experience influences not only the difficulty level of the class but also the ability to comprehend the material, as the newbies encountered more difficulties on both fronts during the entire semester. On the other hand, the values for would_recommend were high in all instances, implying that even though the newbies experienced more obstacles, they still found the class appealing.

Thus, introducing extra resources for beginners may solve the problem while retaining those positive features of the class that attract students. Nevertheless, such adjustments may come at a cost, including money and deterring students who already consider themselves beginners.

Moreover, it will be interesting to determine whether newcomers become better in their performance by the end of the semester and whether some majors struggle more than others.
